12.text: Nvidia hit a record high near $243, authorized a $150B buyback, and reported 106% revenue growth to $96B, with analysts raising targets on strong AI demand. The articles barely mention AMD, bearing on it only as evidence of Nvidia's dominant AI position.

9.text: AMD shares rose 32.3% in a month, and Citi raised its price target 39% while Stifel reiterated Buy ahead of Q3, expecting a beat-and-raise driven by EPYC. Analysts also cited AI-driven CPU demand, 2027 data center growth, and a positive earnings ESP.

7.text: AMD agreed to buy World Labs for $8.2 billion in stock, with founder Fei-Fei Li reporting to CEO Lisa Su. AMD also plans a major 2027 chip supply ramp, pledging tens of billions in Taiwan, as it hit a $1 trillion market cap and HPE launched AMD EPYC-powered servers.

10.text: Chip stocks rallied to three-month highs, then slipped as Broadcom and Applied Materials earnings loomed. TSMC's Q3 sales beat estimates; Musk's talks to bring TSMC into Terafab pressured Intel, while AMD slipped modestly.

11.text: Tech stocks and chipmakers rallied, with AMD among the names rising as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record highs. Broader market gains were supported by falling oil prices and Treasury yields.

14.text: Wells Fargo remains Overweight on AI/HPC operators Applied Digital, TeraWulf, and Hut 8 as they prepare to borrow over $20 billion, with tenant credit and delivery schedules key. AMD isn't mentioned; the story bears on it only as broader AI datacenter demand context.

15.text: HPE landed a $1.2 billion AMD Helios AI rack order from Vultr, launched four new AMD-powered enterprise servers, and raised its fiscal 2027 networking growth and Juniper savings targets. HPE stock hit record highs on the AI demand.

8.text: HPE hit a 52-week high as its AI infrastructure business grows while its valuation remains below peers. The articles barely mention AMD, so the story bears on it only indirectly through shared AI server demand.

13.text: Applied Materials and AMD offer different AI semiconductor exposure, with Applied Materials trading at a lower P/E (23.4x) and improving growth. The comparison weighs which stock is the better buy for 2026.
